notes: Hand compound (2026-09-02, third build), placed from the proxy-fitted truth profile rather than derived: the derivation over a 14 m taper spent its eight parts on the spire and lost the terrace ledges (coverage 0.948, overshoot 0.59 on the second build). Two things shaped it. The slabs are THREE-STEP REDENTED squares, and an axis-aligned box over one stands 1.5-1.9 m above the step below in the six cut-back cells at every corner (~3 m2 per slab), so the niche storey is a CROSS of two boxes on the plan's face flats (3.00 x 1.89 and 1.89 x 3.00, zero overshoot; the three retained corner cells sit over the plinth box as an undershoot), and the plinth (3.00) and cornice (2.87) boxes are held INSIDE the slab below their corners rather than at the slab's own half-width, so what they stand over is a 0.2 m step and not a 1.9 m drop. Second, the self-check casts its rays against a cylinder's BOUNDING SQUARE (heightAt tests |x| and |z| only), so a wide bell cylinder is charged for corners the runtime shape does not have: a 2.63 foot cylinder topped at the torus (3.74) measured 12% overshoot on its own. The foot therefore stops at 3.58 (0.28 above the plinth ring it stands over) and the bell is one cylinder at the proxy's 6.40 m radius, 1.90, whose square corners fall inside the bell's own footprint; the price is the flare below 6.4 m being 0.46 m proud of the proxy at foot level. The harmika box stops at the cap top, 8.93: the spire and finial are covered from below (coverage counts any compound hit) and nothing can stand on them. The aedicules (0.43 m proud of the storey) are not boxed: the plinth box beneath them covers their footprint. The upper slab's 3.30 ledge is 0.18 m above the cornice box top and the plinth ring 0.12 m below the foot part: both inside the 0.30 m step a player takes, both reported as lost by the 0.10 m rule.
